rituals.goal: Catch the instant an unchosen thought begins.
rituals.mission: Catch the instant an unchosen thought begins.
rituals.play: Rest on one neutral point. When a thought appears by itself, catch only its first instant before following it.
rituals.twist: Classify only its form—word, image, memory, plan, sensation—then release.
rituals.win: You notice an arrival before it becomes a complete thought.
rituals.mindBend: A spontaneous thought has a beginning you can catch, separating the arrival of mental content from the act of choosing it.
rituals.mind_bend: A spontaneous thought has a beginning you can catch, separating the arrival of mental content from the act of choosing it.
rituals.safety: Use only one ordinary thought. If forced mental blankness appears, stop and look at a physical object nearby.

rituals.goal: Catch the instant a thought stops being present.

rituals.goal: Let only word one enter the round.
rituals.mission: Let only word one enter the round.

rituals.goal: Allow thought one but deny it a sequel.
rituals.mission: Allow thought one but deny it a sequel.
rituals.rule: The first thought is permitted in full.
rituals.one_rule: The first thought is permitted in full.
rituals.play: Let one thought finish. For the next five seconds, any explanation, defence, prediction or replay counts as a sequel and gets no continuation.
rituals.twist: A genuinely unrelated thought may enter.
rituals.win: The original thought ends without becoming a chain.
rituals.mindBend: The first thought and its explanatory sequel are separate events; rumination begins in what gets added after the thought is already complete.
rituals.mind_bend: The first thought and its explanatory sequel are separate events; rumination begins in what gets added after the thought is already complete.
rituals.safety: Keep this to everyday mental content. When compulsive thought monitoring appears, step out and move back to everyday activity.

rituals.name: QUEUE MASTER
rituals.unique_game_move: serialize simultaneous thought arrivals
rituals.recognition_cue: Mental overload. ROUTER TAGS: overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load
rituals.immediate_need: reduce what the mind has to hold at once
rituals.match_reason: Mental overload; THOUGHT STREAM; ROUTER TAGS: overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load
rituals.goal: Force multiple arrivals into a one-at-a-time queue.
rituals.mission: Force multiple arrivals into a one-at-a-time queue.
rituals.rule: Only one item can occupy the front slot.
rituals.one_rule: Only one item can occupy the front slot.
rituals.play: When several thoughts compete, imagine numbered tickets. Process only the lowest number for three beats; all others wait silently.
rituals.twist: After three beats, move the front ticket to the back without solving it.
rituals.win: Competition becomes an orderly sequence rather than a pile-up.
rituals.mindBend: Mental overload can come from simultaneous competition, not sheer quantity; sequencing the arrivals changes the pressure without deleting any of them.
rituals.mind_bend: Mental overload can come from simultaneous competition, not sheer quantity; sequencing the arrivals changes the pressure without deleting any of them.
rituals.safety: Choose everyday mental content. When greater thought preoccupation appears, end the round; do something simple and concrete.

rituals.goal: Pop only the newest item from awareness.
rituals.mission: Pop only the newest item from awareness.
rituals.play: When several thoughts are active, identify the one that arrived last. Let only that newest item fade or leave; do nothing to earlier items.
rituals.twist: Repeat once only if another clear newest item exists.
rituals.win: You experience mental load decreasing by last-in-first-out removal.
rituals.mindBend: The newest mental item can be released while older material remains. Relief does not always require solving the oldest issue first.
rituals.mind_bend: The newest mental item can be released while older material remains. Relief does not always require solving the oldest issue first.
rituals.safety: Work only with a brief thought sample for one pass. If forced mental blankness develops, pause the exercise and allow the mind to continue without forcing it.

rituals.goal: Count loops only when the same mental job repeats.
rituals.mission: Count loops only when the same mental job repeats.
rituals.rule: Wording changes do not create a new loop.
rituals.one_rule: Wording changes do not create a new loop.

display.mindBend: Boxing every word turns a smooth sentence into separate units. Visual grouping helps the mind fuse individual tokens into one continuous message.
display.safety: Use one manageable sentence for this pass. When the exercise shifts into more threatening text, end it there and let the language sit without further changes.
display.fullRitual:
GAME
BOX EVERY WORD

GOAL
Break a sentence into discrete visual units.

ONE RULE
Boxes may not touch.

PLAY
Render the words in order, each surrounded by a separate small box.

TWIST
Leave tiny gaps between boxes.

WIN
Continuous language becomes a chain of bounded items.

MIND BEND
Boxing every word turns a smooth sentence into separate units. Visual grouping helps the mind fuse individual tokens into one continuous message.

SAFETY
Use one manageable sentence for this pass. When the exercise shifts into more threatening text, end it there and let the language sit without further changes.

rituals.name: PHONEMIC RESTORATION
rituals.unique_game_move: replace one phoneme in a familiar spoken word with imagined noise and observe whether the missing speech sound is perceptually filled in
rituals.recognition_cue: Inner speech • Overthinking. ROUTER TAGS: inner speech self talk self-talk words voice mental text wording inner speech self talk self-talk words voice mental text wording inner speech self talk self-talk words voice mental text wording
rituals.immediate_need: change the relationship to inner wording
rituals.match_reason: Inner speech • Overthinking; INNER SPEECH; ROUTER TAGS: inner speech self talk self-talk words voice mental text wording inner speech self talk self-talk words voice mental text wording inner speech self talk self-talk words voice mental text wording
rituals.goal: Make the mind hear a speech sound that was never played.
rituals.mission: Make the mind hear a speech sound that was never played.
rituals.rule: One speech sound is replaced by noise, not silence.
rituals.one_rule: One speech sound is replaced by noise, not silence.
rituals.play: Hear the word LEGAL internally, but replace the G sound with a brief imagined cough/noise burst. Notice whether the word still seems complete.
rituals.twist: Do not consciously insert the missing phoneme.
rituals.win: Language context can perceptually restore a speech sound hidden by noise.

PHONEMIC RESTORATION

GOAL
Make the mind hear a speech sound that was never played.

ONE RULE
One speech sound is replaced by noise, not silence.

PLAY

TWIST
Do not consciously insert the missing phoneme.

WIN
Language context can perceptually restore a speech sound hidden by noise.

rituals.goal: See whether your own choice quietly becomes your population estimate.
rituals.mission: See whether your own choice quietly becomes your population estimate.
rituals.rule: Preference and prevalence are two separate answers.
rituals.one_rule: Preference and prevalence are two separate answers.
rituals.play: Choose tea or coffee. Then estimate, out of 100 random adults, how many would make the same choice. Notice whether your own preference pulls the estimate upward.
rituals.twist: Keep the population estimate separate from whether your own choice is better.
rituals.win: Personal preference and assumed social prevalence become distinct judgements.
rituals.mindBend: Personal preference can inflate estimates of how many other people agree. False consensus is projection from ‘I choose this’ to ‘most people probably would too’.
rituals.mind_bend: Personal preference can inflate estimates of how many other people agree. False consensus is projection from ‘I choose this’ to ‘most people probably would too’.
rituals.safety: Use a trivial preference with no social stakes. If the estimate starts feeding certainty about what other people think or becomes a self-worth comparison, stop and return to observable facts.

rituals.mission: Change which word carries the sentence's spotlight.

rituals.goal: Make separate sounds snap into one word.
rituals.mission: Make separate sounds snap into one word.
rituals.rule: Keep the three sounds distinct until the blend.
rituals.one_rule: Keep the three sounds distinct until the blend.
rituals.play: Hear /k/ ... /a/ ... /t/ separately in inner speech. Then shorten the gaps until the three sounds fuse into CAT.
rituals.twist: Do not add any extra sound between them.
rituals.win: Three separate phonemes become one recognised word through temporal blending.
rituals.mindBend: Separate speech sounds can fuse into a single word percept without any sound being changed. Lexical meaning is an emergent result of ordered phoneme combination.
rituals.mind_bend: Separate speech sounds can fuse into a single word percept without any sound being changed. Lexical meaning is an emergent result of ordered phoneme combination.
rituals.safety: Work only with manageable inner wording for one pass. If compulsive sentence repetition develops, stop the exercise; use external text as the reference.

rituals.goal: Repeat a word until it starts sounding strangely like sound.
rituals.mission: Repeat a word until it starts sounding strangely like sound.
rituals.rule: Use one neutral word and keep the pace steady.
rituals.one_rule: Use one neutral word and keep the pace steady.
rituals.play: Pick the neutral word WINDOW. Repeat it internally around fifteen times at a quick, even pace. When the repetitions end, check whether the sound briefly feels stranger than its meaning.
rituals.twist: Avoid explaining the word while repeating it.
rituals.win: A familiar word can momentarily feel like raw sound after sustained repetition.
rituals.mindBend: Rapid repetition can make a familiar neutral word temporarily sound strange and less meaningful. Meaning is an effect that can weaken while the sound-form stays constant.
rituals.mind_bend: Rapid repetition can make a familiar neutral word temporarily sound strange and less meaningful. Meaning is an effect that can weaken while the sound-form stays constant.
rituals.safety: Choose manageable inner wording. When compulsive sentence repetition becomes noticeable, step out and leave the sentence alone.

rituals.goal: See whether the mind notices when its choice label is secretly switched.
rituals.mission: See whether the mind notices when its choice label is secretly switched.
rituals.rule: Use trivial options with no real consequence.
rituals.one_rule: Use trivial options with no real consequence.
rituals.play: Choose mentally between ○ and △. Hide both for one beat. Now deliberately tell yourself 'I chose' followed by the opposite symbol and notice whether a mismatch signal appears.
rituals.twist: Do not rationalise the switched choice; only notice detection or non-detection.
rituals.win: Choice memory and the label attached to it can be tested as separate processes.
rituals.mindBend: A person may sometimes accept a relabelled opposite option as the choice they made. Choice blindness can recruit post-hoc reasoning to defend a mismatched outcome.
rituals.mind_bend: A person may sometimes accept a relabelled opposite option as the choice they made. Choice blindness can recruit post-hoc reasoning to defend a mismatched outcome.
rituals.safety: Use a short look at thinking for this task. If recursive self-monitoring appears, end there; shift attention outward.

rituals.goal: Test whether 'I know how it works' survives an explanation attempt.
rituals.mission: Test whether 'I know how it works' survives an explanation attempt.
rituals.rule: Explain mechanism steps, not purpose or labels.
rituals.one_rule: Explain mechanism steps, not purpose or labels.
rituals.play: Pick something familiar such as a zipper or toilet flush. Rate understanding 0–10, explain exactly how the mechanism works step by step, then rate again.
rituals.twist: Any 'and then it just works' step counts as a missing mechanism.
rituals.win: Perceived understanding can shrink when hidden explanatory gaps are forced into view.
rituals.mindBend: Trying to explain every causal link in a familiar mechanism exposes where apparent understanding relies on an unexplained jump.
rituals.mind_bend: Trying to explain every causal link in a familiar mechanism exposes where apparent understanding relies on an unexplained jump.
rituals.safety: Use only a short look at thinking. Stop at once if analysis of every mental event appears; shift attention outward.

rituals.goal: Ask what would happen if you actively changed the suspected cause.
rituals.mission: Ask what would happen if you actively changed the suspected cause.
rituals.rule: An intervention changes the candidate cause rather than merely observing it.
rituals.one_rule: An intervention changes the candidate cause rather than merely observing it.
rituals.play: Use a harmless example: coffee drinking and alertness rise together. Imagine actively setting coffee to zero while sleep and time of day stay the same. Ask what each causal story predicts.
rituals.twist: Do not treat correlation alone as the intervention result.
rituals.win: A causal claim becomes testable by what should change under deliberate intervention.
rituals.mindBend: Correlation becomes more informative about causation only when a candidate cause is deliberately changed while other relevant conditions are held steady. Intervention is a stronger test than observation.
rituals.mind_bend: Correlation becomes more informative about causation only when a candidate cause is deliberately changed while other relevant conditions are held steady. Intervention is a stronger test than observation.
rituals.safety: Use only a harmless, checkable claim. If real safety information is being dismissed, stop the thought experiment and verify the situation with an appropriate person or reliable source before continuing.

rituals.goal: Catch a detailed story feeling more likely than its broader parent event.
rituals.mission: Catch a detailed story feeling more likely than its broader parent event.
rituals.rule: The specific option includes every condition of the broad option plus one more.
rituals.one_rule: The specific option includes every condition of the broad option plus one more.
rituals.play: Which is more likely: A) a person works in a bank, or B) a person works in a bank and volunteers for an environmental group? Choose before analysing.
rituals.twist: Then apply the set rule: A includes all cases in B plus additional bank workers.
rituals.win: A vivid conjunction can feel more probable despite being mathematically a subset of the broader event.
rituals.mindBend: A specific conjunction cannot be more probable than the broader event containing it; vivid detail can nevertheless make the narrower story feel more convincing.
rituals.mind_bend: A specific conjunction cannot be more probable than the broader event containing it; vivid detail can nevertheless make the narrower story feel more convincing.
rituals.safety: Keep this to low-stakes examples. If real safety facts start being discounted, end the exercise and seek appropriate real-world verification or professional assessment rather than reasoning past those facts.

rituals.goal: Flip a rule without changing its logic.
rituals.mission: Flip a rule without changing its logic.
rituals.rule: Reverse the direction and negate both parts.
rituals.one_rule: Reverse the direction and negate both parts.
rituals.play: Use: 'If it is a square, it has four sides.' Form the contrapositive: 'If it does not have four sides, it is not a square.'
rituals.twist: Do not confuse it with simply reversing the original rule.
rituals.win: One logical relationship is preserved through a precise structural transformation.
rituals.mindBend: ‘If P then Q’ logically guarantees ‘if not Q then not P’. That clarifies why the contraposition is equivalent while simply reversing the original rule is not.
rituals.mind_bend: ‘If P then Q’ logically guarantees ‘if not Q then not P’. That clarifies why the contraposition is equivalent while simply reversing the original rule is not.
rituals.safety: Limit this to a bounded belief question. If frightening unverifiable interpretations appear, do not continue; use shared evidence rather than solitary certainty.

rituals.goal: Decide whether new information should make you stay or switch.
rituals.mission: Decide whether new information should make you stay or switch.
rituals.rule: The host always reveals a losing door you did not choose.
rituals.one_rule: The host always reveals a losing door you did not choose.
rituals.play: Pick Door 1 from three doors. The host, who knows the prize, opens Door 3 and shows no prize. Decide whether to stay with Door 1 or switch to Door 2.
rituals.twist: Track where the original 2/3 probability mass can go after the host's forced reveal.
rituals.win: Switching captures the original probability carried by the two unchosen doors and wins with probability 2/3.
rituals.mindBend: When the host is forced to reveal a losing door, the original two-thirds probability does not vanish; it concentrates on the remaining unchosen door, making switching rational.

rituals.safety: Keep this to ordinary low-stakes evidence. When frightening unverifiable interpretations appear, step out and use external verification.

rituals.goal: Count the invisible jumps between fact and conclusion.
rituals.mission: Count the invisible jumps between fact and conclusion.
rituals.rule: Each unsupported leap counts as one step.
rituals.one_rule: Each unsupported leap counts as one step.
rituals.play: Use a mild example: FACT='They replied late.' CONCLUSION='They are angry with me.' Name every extra assumption needed to get from the fact to the conclusion and count them.
rituals.twist: Do not decide whether the conclusion is true; count only the bridge steps.
rituals.win: A conclusion becomes visibly separated from observation by its inference distance.

rituals.finalRitual:
GAME
INFERENCE STEP COUNT

GOAL
Count the invisible jumps between fact and conclusion.

ONE RULE
Each unsupported leap counts as one step.

PLAY
Use a mild example: FACT='They replied late.' CONCLUSION='They are angry with me.' Name every extra assumption needed to get from the fact to the conclusion and count them.

TWIST
Do not decide whether the conclusion is true; count only the bridge steps.

WIN
A conclusion becomes visibly separated from observation by its inference distance.
